claims.text: GDACS's event report (eventid 1029794, episode 15, GLIDE WF-2026-000131-ESP) assessed an Orange alert for medium humanitarian impact for a wildfire in the Plana Baixa comarca, Castellón province, Spain, covering a 25-30 July 2026 window, citing about 13,370 hectares burned and roughly 19,334 people in the fire-affected area.

The European Union's Copernicus Earth-observation programme states that Spain's government declared a national emergency on 23 July 2026 in response to multiple simultaneous large wildfires, and that more than 100,000 people have been evacuated or instructed to remain indoors across the affected Spanish regions combined.

Re-checked 4 August 2026: GDACS's event report (eventid 1029794) still shows episode 15 (25-30 July 2026 window) as the latest, with no newer episode published and the most recent thermal-anomaly detection unchanged at 30 July 2026 — five days with no new hotspot activity. Burned area and affected population remain about 13,370 hectares and 19,334 people.

description: A wildfire broke out in the Plana Baixa comarca of Castellón province, Spain, around 25 July 2026, north of Valencia — a separate outbreak from the concurrent, larger fire complex burning southwest of Madrid and in Ávila province. GDACS assessed the event at an Orange alert for medium humanitarian impact, citing about 13,370 hectares burned and roughly 19,334 people in the fire-affected area over a 25-30 July 2026 window. Spain's government had declared a national emergency on 23 July 2026 in response to the country's simultaneous large wildfires, with more than 100,000 people evacuated or instructed to remain indoors across the affected regions combined. The fire produced no new detectable hotspot activity after 30 July 2026 and is considered contained.

impact.summary: GDACS's event report (episode 15) assessed an Orange alert for medium humanitarian impact, citing about 13,370 hectares burned and roughly 19,334 people in the fire-affected area over a 25-30 July 2026 window; no thermal anomaly has been detected since 30 July, and the fire is considered contained. Spain's national emergency, declared 23 July 2026 amid simultaneous large wildfires, saw more than 100,000 people evacuated or instructed to remain indoors across the affected Spanish regions combined — a combined, not Castellón-specific, figure. No confirmed death toll has been published for this fire specifically.
